targets.name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
targets.description: The best-lit point of the ridge that joins Shackleton and de Gerlache craters at the lunar south pole (88% mean illumination 2 m above the ground). A representative site of the polar highlands, not a declared base location.
targets.coordinate_note: Connecting Ridge site C1, the best-lit point of the ridge.

temp_annual_range.note: Diviner polar cumulative product: summer minus winter bolometric temperature, from 192 local-time files (96 per season).

temp_diurnal_range.note: Diviner polar cumulative product, day minus night bolometric temperature.

mean_temperature.note: Diviner polar cumulative product, mean of all local times and both seasons.

composition.uncertainty: medium: the nearest class available, not an exact match
composition.note: Anorthositic highlands mapped to felsic, the nearest of the four classes. Anorthosite is rich in calcic plagioclase and poorer in silica than granite, so the site sheet must show this limit.

elevation.note: LOLA, relative to the lunar reference radius. Context only.

targets.name: Arcadia Planitia
targets.description: Northern plain of Mars where SHARAD radar and terraced craters show a wide layer of excess ice a few metres or less below the surface. The representative point is the 'Badger' crater of Bramson et al. 2015 (46.58 N, 194.85 E), inside their study area of 38 to 50 N and 180 to 225 E.
targets.coordinate_note: Crater 'Badger', Bramson et al. 2015, converted to -180 to 180 east.

slope.uncertainty: p10 0.06 to p90 0.47 degrees (pixels in the window)
slope.note: MOLA MEGDR at 128 pixels per degree.

roughness.uncertainty: p10 0.5 to p90 2.7 m (pixels in the window)
roughness.note: MOLA MEGDR at 128 pixels per degree.

temp_annual_range.note: Mars Climate Database surface temperature: warmest minus coldest seasonal daily mean. A model, so basis is literature.

temp_diurnal_range.note: Mars Climate Database surface temperature, day minus night. A model, so basis is literature.

mean_temperature.note: Mars Climate Database mean surface temperature. A model, so basis is literature.

composition.uncertainty: medium: the area mixes volcanic units (Av, 12 of 25 points) and sedimentary ones (lHl, 6 of 25)
composition.note: SIM 3292 (Tanaka et al. 2014) puts the Badger point in unit Av, lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows, which the rule maps to basaltic. The earlier sedimentary (lHl) choice is not supported at this point.

elevation.note: MOLA, relative to the Mars datum. Context only.

targets.name: Jezero crater
targets.description: Impact crater about 45 to 49 km wide on the western edge of Isidis Planitia that held a lake and a delta about 3.5 billion years ago. Perseverance has worked there since February 2021 at Octavia E. Butler Landing. The floor is basaltic and ultramafic igneous rock, with a sedimentary delta to the west.
targets.coordinate_note: Coordinates of Octavia E. Butler Landing.

slope.uncertainty: p10 0.4 to p90 8.03 degrees (pixels in the window)
slope.note: MOLA MEGDR at 128 pixels per degree.

roughness.uncertainty: p10 3.0 to p90 51.3 m (pixels in the window)
roughness.note: MOLA MEGDR at 128 pixels per degree.

temp_annual_range.uncertainty: about ±5 K (models differ by up to 10 K in surface temperature around Jezero, Newman et al. 2021; the seasonal range is less sensitive than absolute values)
temp_annual_range.note: Mars Climate Database: warmest minus coldest seasonal daily mean. A model, so basis is literature.

temp_diurnal_range.uncertainty: about ±15 K; MEDA measures smaller swings than the MCD (near Ls 65 MEDA saw about 200 K minimum and 260 K maximum, about 60 K, against about 83 K in the MCD)
temp_diurnal_range.note: Mars Climate Database: day minus night. A model, so basis is literature.

mean_temperature.uncertainty: about ±5 °C (models spread up to 10 K; MEDA is warmer at night and colder by day than the MCD)
mean_temperature.note: Mars Climate Database mean surface temperature. A model, so basis is literature.

composition.uncertainty: dominant class; the western edge of the exploration area is sedimentary (delta)
composition.note: Farley et al. 2022: igneous basaltic and ultramafic crater floor.

elevation.note: MOLA, relative to the Mars datum. Context only.
